description: Real-HA golden divergence ledger (Step 2 #1127). A golden that fails on real Home Assistant must be listed with a class (E environment, F fake artifact, T trigger, P production bug, G golden premise), the failing assertion indexes (-1 = an exception Climate Advisor logged, -2 = a timer left armed after unload) and evidence. An unlisted failure fails; an entry whose scenario now passes, or fails differently, fails. Never edit a golden to remove an entry. failing_outcomes pins WHAT each failing assertion actually produced (assertion index -> actual outcome; -1 -> exception:<types>, -2 -> timer:<callback>), so a worse or different failure of a ledgered assertion fails.

entries.first_difference: a0@2026-08-21T23:19 expected nat_vent_still_active, real natural_ventilation (sensor_opened emitted twice: 23:15 and 23:19)
entries.evidence: The golden's sensor_open carries seed:true, which FakeHass applies with a silent state set so no listener runs and only the 23:19 startup_coalesce sees the open window. Real HA has no silent write: states.async_set always notifies, so the real door/window listener activates nat-vent at 23:15 and the later coalesce re-activates it. The adapter records note 'seed/seed_fresh' on the run. Dump: .pytest_cache/realha/733_restart_reconcile_clobbers_fresh_nat_vent.real.json
entries.occupant_view: Same end state for the person (fan on, window open); only the path to it differs. No occupant impact found.
entries.issue_or_justification: Trigger divergence. The real analog of 'window was already open before HA started' is a state that exists before the listener subscribes, i.e. a real restart with the sensor open; model it with house.restart in a dedicated real-HA test, not by editing this golden.

entries.first_difference: a1@2026-01-15T09:00 expected classification_applied, real comfort_restored (morning_wakeup at 06:30:00)
entries.evidence: Engine-only golden (no use_coordinator): FakeHass has no coordinator, so no daily schedule. Real HA runs the default wake_time 06:30 timer and emits morning_wakeup, which the outcomes layer maps to comfort_restored; the golden asserts 'no new decision after the 06:01 classification'. The event log shows morning_wakeup@06:30:00 only on the real side.
entries.occupant_view: The home restores comfort at the default wake time, as it should; the golden's 'nothing happens until bedtime' premise only holds in a world without the daily schedule.
entries.issue_or_justification: Trigger divergence: the scenario models only its listed events. Not a production defect.

entries.first_difference: a2@2026-07-02T18:53 expected natural_ventilation, real classification_suppressed_paused; a3@18:56 real paused (nat_vent_outdoor_rise_exit at 18:53:00 with indoor 72.0, outdoor 72.0)
entries.evidence: One temp_update carries indoor 75 and outdoor 72. FakeHass applies both, then evaluates once. Real HA delivers them through two listeners; whichever is written first is evaluated against the other's old value. Outdoor-first (current adapter): the outdoor listener sees old indoor 72 vs new outdoor 72 and exits nat-vent. Indoor-first: this scenario passes but bedtime_natvent_continuation and 2026-03-28-overnight fail the same way (experiment run 2026-10-30, reverted).
entries.occupant_view: Two real sensors never update atomically, so the exit can fire on a half-updated pair; the person would see the fan stop and the window-open pause start for about 2 minutes before the next reading re-engages it.
entries.issue_or_justification: Trigger/environment divergence: the golden's atomic two-reading update has no real-HA equivalent. Whether CA should ride out one stale partner reading is a separate design question for the owner; no issue filed.

entries.first_difference: a2@2026-03-28T20:00 expected paused, real morning_wakeup_skipped (morning_wakeup at 06:30:00.275); a3@2026-03-28T23:30 expected paused, real bedtime_setback_skipped (bedtime at 22:30:00.275)
entries.evidence: Issue #1140 re-signed this golden: the install has no fan, so the 20:00 window open pauses HVAC instead of starting windows-only nat-vent, and the scenario's last event-driven decision is 'paused'. FakeHass models only the listed events, so 'paused' stays the last decision. Real HA also runs the default daily schedule (wake 06:30, bedtime 22:30), which emits morning_wakeup_skipped / bedtime_setback_skipped because the pause is in force; the outcomes layer is last-decision-wins, so those are what a2/a3 see. Real log: 'Door/window pause (binary_sensor.door_window): HVAC already off - pause flag set'. Dump: .pytest_cache/realha/2026-03-28-overnight.real.json
entries.occupant_view: Same end state for the person: HVAC stays off while the window is open, and the wake-up and bedtime routines correctly skip. No occupant impact.
entries.issue_or_justification: Trigger divergence (daily schedule not modeled by the scenario), same mechanism as cool_all_day_heat_all_day and warm_day_planned_window_no_fan_pauses. Not a production defect.

entries.first_difference: a1@2026-08-23T22:30 expected bedtime_setback_skipped, real hvac_write_blocked_whf_active (nat-vent reactivated at the 20:10 revisit refresh, so _paused_by_door is False at bedtime)
entries.evidence: Issue #1337: the real-HA house has no weather entity, and a refresh with no forecast used to run nothing. It now runs the weather-independent cycle, including the regular-cycle check_natural_vent_conditions() while a sensor is open and a real outdoor reading exists (the scenario's 74F). At the 20:10 five-minute revisit refresh that check reactivates nat-vent over the door pause ('Natural vent activated ... while paused'), exactly what the same refresh does in production with a weather entity. FakeHass dispatches no revisit refresh, so Tier A still reaches bedtime paused_by_door. Assertions 2 (economizer still cool-down) and 3 (AC never commanded) pass on real HA. Dump: .pytest_cache/realha/issue_764_bedtime_economizer_teardown_gate.real.json
entries.occupant_view: Same outcome for the person: the whole-house fan keeps free-cooling through bedtime and the AC never starts. Only the reason bedtime leaves HVAC alone differs (WHF owns HVAC instead of the door pause).
entries.issue_or_justification: Trigger divergence (#1337). The real tier now runs the revisit refresh the way production does; the golden's assertion 1 describes the FakeHass path with no such refresh. Not a production bug; do not edit the golden.

entries.first_difference: a1@2026-07-17T02:30 expected pre_cool_applied 69, real setback_applied (no 02:30 write)
entries.evidence: Since #1420 the scenario's pre_cool event no longer calls handle_pre_cool a second time when the coordinator's own 02:30 trigger fired in that minute; that trigger is production's only pre-cool. The real trigger fired and logged 'Pre-cool trigger fired: skipped - the day this night wakes into is not pre-cool eligible': after midnight it re-checks eligibility on the day the night wakes into (#1378, owner decision), which needs today_high/today_low on the classification (warming trend against the recorded previous-day highs) or today_high >= the hot threshold. This scenario's hand-fed classification carries only day_type warm and setback_modifier -3.0, no highs, so the fire-time re-check cannot hold. Before #1420 the direct handler call (which skips that re-check) wrote 69 and hid this. Dump: .pytest_cache/realha/warming_trend_pre_cool_applied.real.json
entries.occupant_view: No occupant impact found: a real install's classification always carries the forecast highs the re-check reads (the sibling hot_plateau_pre_cool_applied and hot_night_same_mode_pre_cool_wakeup_keeps_cool_1417 carry them and pre-cool on real HA). Only this scenario's premise lacks them.
entries.issue_or_justification: Golden premise: the scenario models the pre-cool as an engine call and omits the forecast highs production's own trigger reads at fire time. The Tier A run (engine-only, no trigger) still exercises handle_pre_cool's target. Fix by giving the classification today_high/today_low/tomorrow_high (owner re-sign), not by restoring the double dispatch.
